body.translated_text: <s>Svalpākṣarā Prajñāpāramitā</s> (The Perfection of Wisdom in Few Syllables)

body.text: evaṃ mayā śrutam | ekasmin samaye bhagavān rājagṛhe viharati sma gṛdhrakūṭe parvate mahatā bhikṣusaṃghena sārdhaṃ dvādaśasāhasrapañcaśatairbodhisattvakoṭiniyutaśatasahasraiḥ sārdhaṃ viharati sma, lokapālādidevakoṭiniyutasahasraiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛtaḥ śrīsiṃhāsane viharati sma ||
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time, the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) was dwelling at <s>Rājagṛha</s>, on <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> (Vulture Peak) mountain, together with a great assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks) numbering twelve thousand five hundred, together with hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of <s>niyutas</s> (millions) of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, surrounded and honored by thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>niyutas</s> of <s>devas</s> (gods) headed by the <s>Lokapālas</s> (World-Protectors), dwelling upon a glorious lion-throne.

body.text: atha khalu bodhisattvo mahāsattvo āryāvalokiteśvaro utthāya āsanādekamaṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya prahasitavadano bhūtvā bhagavantametadavocat - deśayatu bhagavān prajñāpāramitāṃ svalpākṣarāṃ mahāpuṇyām, yasyāḥ śravaṇamātreṇa sarvasattvāḥ sarvakarmāvaraṇāni kṣapayiṣyanti, niyataṃ ca bodhiparāyaṇā bhaviṣyanti | ye ca sattvā mantrasādhane udyuktāsteṣāṃ cāvighnena mantrāḥ sidhyanti ||
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> (great being) <s>Āryāvalokiteśvara</s>, rising from his seat, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, placing his right knee on the ground, joining his palms in reverence toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and with a smiling face, spoke thus to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'May the <s>Bhagavān</s> teach the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom) in few syllables, of great merit, by merely hearing which all beings shall exhaust all <s>karmāvaraṇas</s> (karmic obscurations), and shall certainly become destined for <s>bodhi</s> (awakening). And for those beings who are engaged in <s>mantrasādhana</s> (mantra practice), their <s>mantras</s> shall succeed without obstruction.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākaruṇikāya sādhukāramadāt - sādhu sādhu kulaputra, yastvaṃ sarvasattvānāmarthāya hitāya sukhāya pradhānāya ca dīrgharātraṃ niyuktaḥ | tena hi tvaṃ kulaputra śṛṇu, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuru | bhāṣiṣye 'haṃ te prajñāpāramitāṃ svalpākṣarāṃ mahāpuṇyām, yasyāḥ śravaṇamātreṇa sarvasattvāḥ sarvakarmāvaraṇāni kṣapayiṣyanti, niyataṃ ca bodhiparāyaṇā bhaviṣyanti | ye ca sattvā mantrasādhane udyuktāsteṣāṃ cāvighnenaḥ mantrāḥ sidhyanti ||
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> gave his approval to the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Āryāvalokiteśvara</s>, the greatly compassionate one: 'Excellent, excellent, O son of good family! You who have long been devoted to the welfare, benefit, happiness, and supreme good of all beings. Therefore, O son of good family, listen well and attend carefully. I shall teach you the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> in few syllables, of great merit, by merely hearing which all beings shall exhaust all <s>karmāvaraṇas</s> (karmic obscurations), and shall certainly become destined for <s>bodhi</s> (awakening). And for those beings who are engaged in <s>mantrasādhana</s> (mantra practice), their <s>mantras</s> shall succeed without obstruction.'

body.text: atha khalu āryāvalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - tena hi sugata bhāṣatu sarvasattvānāmarthāya hitāya sukhāya ca ||
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Āryāvalokiteśvara</s> spoke thus to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Then, O <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One), please speak for the welfare, benefit, and happiness of all beings.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāṃ sarvaduḥkhapramocano nāma samādhiṃ samāpadyate sma, yasya ca samādhiṃ samāpannasya bhagavata ūrṇākośavivarāllavādanekāni raśmikoṭiniyutaśatasahasrāṇi niścaranti sma | taiśca raśmibhiḥ sarvabuddhakṣetrāṇi parisphuṭānyabhūvan | ye ca sattvāstayā prabhayā spṛṣṭāḥ, te sarve niyatā abhūvannanuttarāya samyaksaṃbodhau | yāvannārakāḥ sattvāḥ * * *sarve ca buddhakṣetrāṇi ṣaḍvikāraṃ praviceluḥ | divyāni ca candanacūrṇavarṣāṇi tathāgatapādamūlaṃ vavarṣuḥ ||
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, at that time, entered the <s>samādhi</s> (meditative concentration) called '<s>Sarvaduḥkhapramocana</s>' (Liberation from All Suffering). And when the <s>Bhagavān</s> had entered that <s>samādhi</s>, from the opening of his <s>ūrṇākośa</s> (hair-curl between the eyebrows) there emerged many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>niyutas</s> of rays of light. By those rays, all <s>buddhakṣetras</s> (buddha-fields) were illuminated. And all those beings who were touched by that radiance became certain of attaining <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening), even those beings in the hells. And all the <s>buddhakṣetras</s> trembled in six ways. And divine showers of sandalwood powder rained down at the feet of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ bhāṣate sma | tadyathā - bodhisattvena mahāsattvena samacittena bhavitavyam | sarvasattveṣu maitracittena bhavitavyam | kṛtajñena bhavitavyam | kṛtavedinā ca bhavitavyam | sarvapāpaviratacittena bhavitavyam | idaṃ ca prajñāpāramitāhṛdayamāgrahītavyam - namo ratnatrayāya | namaḥ śākyamunaye tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya | tadyathā - oṃ mune mune mahāmunaye svāhā || asyāḥ prajñāpāramitāyā lābhāt mayā anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhiranuprāptā | sarvabuddhāśca ato niryātāḥ || mayā api iyameva (

children.text: ) prajñāpāramitā śrutā mahāśākyamunestathāgatasya sākṣāt | tena hi tvaṃ sarvabodhisattvānāmagrato buddhatve ca vyākṛtaḥ - bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ māṇava anāgate 'dhvani sa(mantaraśmisamu)dgataḥ śrīkūṭarājā nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān | [badiyamapi?] ye idaṃ nāmadheyaṃ śroṣyanti dhārayiṣyanti vācayiṣyanti likhayayiṣyanti, parebhyaśca vistareṇa saṃprakāśayiṣyanti, pustakalikhitamapi kṛtvā gṛhe dhārayiṣyanti pūjayiṣyanti, te sarve alpopāyena alpaśravaṇena ca tathāgatā bhaviṣyanti | tadyathā - oṃ jeya jeya padmābhe avame avame sarasaraṇi dhiridhiri devatā anupālani yuddhottāriṇi paracakranivāriṇi pūraya pūraya bhagavati sarva āśā mama ca sarvasattvānāṃ ca | sarvakarmāvaraṇāni viśodhaya, buddhādhiṣṭhite svāhā || iyaṃ sā kulaputra paramārthaprajñāpāramitā sarvabuddhānāṃ jananī bodhisattvamātā (bodhidātrī) pāpahārakā | sarvabuddhairapi na śaknoti asyānuśaṃsā vaktuṃ yāvatkalpakoṭiśatairapi | anayā paṭhitamātreṇa sarvaparṣanmaṇḍalābhiṣiktā bhavanti, sarve ca mantrāḥ abhimukhā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom) was heard directly from the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the great <s>Śākyamuni</s>. By him you were prophesied to <s>Buddhahood</s> before all <s>Bodhisattvas</s>: "You, O youth, in a future age shall become a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Samantaraśmisamudgata Śrīkūṭarāja</s>, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One), Knower of the World, Unsurpassed, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One." Moreover, those who shall hear, retain, recite, and cause to be written this name, and who shall explain it in detail to others, and who, having had it written in a book, shall keep and worship it in their homes — all of them, through small means and little hearing, shall become <s>Tathāgatas</s>. The <s>dhāraṇī</s> is as follows: <s>Oṃ jeya jeya padmābhe avame avame sarasaraṇi dhiridhiri devatā anupālani yuddhottāriṇi paracakranivāriṇi pūraya pūraya bhagavati sarva āśā mama ca sarvasattvānāṃ ca sarva karmāvaraṇāni viśodhaya buddhādhiṣṭhite svāhā</s>. This, O son of good family, is the ultimate <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom), the mother of all <s>Buddhas</s>, the mother of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, the bestower of awakening, the remover of sin. Even all the <s>Buddhas</s> are unable to declare her benefits even in hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> (ten millions) of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons). By merely reciting her, one becomes consecrated in all assemblies, and all <s>mantras</s> become favorable.

body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, at that time, spoke the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. That is to say: A <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> should abide with an equal mind. One should abide with a mind of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) toward all beings. One should be grateful. One should be appreciative. One should abide with a mind that has ceased from all evil. And one should grasp this heart of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>: Homage to the <s>Triratna</s> (Three Jewels). Homage to <s>Śākyamuni Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s> (Worthy One), the perfectly and fully awakened one. That is: Oṃ mune mune mahāmunaye svāhā. Through the attainment of this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, I have attained <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening). And all <s>Buddhas</s> have proceeded from this. By me also, this very (

body.text: atha āryāvalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - kena kāraṇena bhagavan iyaṃ svalpākṣarā prajñāpāramitā? bhagavānāha - alpopāyatvāt | ye 'pi sattvā mandāsvādāḥ, te 'pi imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ svalpākṣarāṃ dhārayiṣyanti vācayiṣyanti likhiṣyanti likhayiṣyanti, te sarve alpopāyena bodhiparāyaṇā bhaviṣyanti | anena kāraṇena kulaputra iyaṃ saṃkṣiptā svalpākṣarā prajñāpāramitā ||
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, said this to the Blessed One: "For what reason, O Blessed One, is this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> called 'in few syllables' (<s>Svalpākṣarā</s>)?" The Blessed One replied: "Because of the smallness of the means. Even those beings who are of dull capacity shall retain, recite, write, and cause to be written this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> in Few Syllables, and all of them, through small means, shall become destined for awakening (<s>bodhiparāyaṇa</s>). For this reason, O son of good family, this is the condensed <s>Svalpākṣarā Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom in Few Syllables)."

body.text: evamukte āryāvalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - āścaryaṃ bhagavan, paramāścaryaṃ sugata, yāvadeva bhagavān sarvasattvahitāya ayaṃ dharmaparyāyo bhāṣito mandapudgalānāmeva arthāya hitāya sukhāya ceti ||
body.translated_text: When this was said, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, said this to the Blessed One: "It is wonderful, O Blessed One! Most wonderful, O <s>Sugata</s>! Insofar as the Blessed One has spoken this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse on the Dharma) for the benefit of all beings, for the sake, welfare, and happiness of those of dull faculties!"

body.text: idamavocadbhagavān | āttamanā āryāvalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ, te ca bhikṣavaste ca bodhisattvāḥ sā ca sarvāvatī parṣat sadevamānuṣāsuragandharvaśca loko bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandanniti ||
body.translated_text: Thus spoke the Blessed One. The <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, was delighted, and those <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks) and those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and that entire assembly, together with the world of <s>devas</s> (gods), humans, <s>asuras</s> (demons), and <s>gandharvas</s> (celestial musicians), rejoiced at the words of the Blessed One.
The <s>Svalpākṣarā Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom in Few Syllables) is completed.
